'''''Hyparrhenia''''' is a genus of [[Poaceae|grasses]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/393885#page/73/mode/1up Fournier, Eugène Pierre Nicolas. 1886.  Mexicanas Plantas 2: 51, 67] in Latin</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40029728 Tropicos, ''Hyparrhenia'' Andersson ex E. Fourn]</ref> Many species are known commonly as '''thatching grass'''.<ref>Onana, J.M. (2011). The vascular plants of Cameroon a taxonomic checklist with IUCN assessments: 1-195. National herbarium of Cameroon, Yaoundé.</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=116166 Flora of China Vol. 22 Page 631 <big>苞茅属</big> bao mao shu ''Hyparrhenia'' Andersson ex Fournier, Mexic. Pl. 2: 51, 67. 1886. ]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=hyparrhenia |title=Altervista Flora Italiana genere hyparrhenia |access-date=2015-02-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201021956/http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Hyparrhenia |archive-date=2015-02-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:417762# Atlas of Living Australia]</ref>

They are mostly native to tropical [[Africa]]; some can be found in warmer areas in temperate [[Eurasia]], [[Australia]], and [[Latin America]]. These are annual and perennial bunch grasses. The [[inflorescence]] branches into twin spikes of paired spikelets.<ref>Filgueiras, T. S. 1981. O genero ''Hyparrhenia'' (Gramineae) no Brasil. Anais do XXXII Congresso Nacional de Botanica 44–57.</ref><ref>Pohl, R. W. 1994. 164. ''Hyparrhenia'' Andersson ex Fourn. 6: 393–394. In G. Davidse, M. Sousa Sánchez & A.O. Chater (eds.) Flora Mesoamericana. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, México, D.F.</ref><ref>[http://redlist.sanbi.org/genus.php?genus=1217 Sanbi, Red List of South African Plants]</ref>
